properties.name: Brooklyn Hydraulic ground
properties.tier: A — paying gold, abandoned by corporate panic
properties.evidence: F.C. Brooks (manager, 1913 recollection in Haygarth 2022 n.47): sluiced a fortnight for 16 oz 'which paid expenses for the actual time of sluicing'; shut by directors' wire after OTHER companies' poor cleanups, June 1895. Recorded occurrence 'Brooklyn' marks the claim; the paying face was barely opened.

properties.name: New Donaldson Hydraulic ground
properties.evidence: Haygarth 2022 p.44 (n.50): 'after more than a year's infrastructure work, the mine that was going to pay £300 per week was abandoned without its gravels being tested.' The unused 19.4 km head race survives along the Western Explorer. Montgomery (1894, n.29) rated the district's terraces 'undoubtedly an excellent field'.

properties.name: George Town Packet Creek
properties.tier: B — 1881-mapped gold locality, no modern record
properties.status_2026: EL25/2020 — lapses 2 Dec 2026; 129 m from mapped lead
properties.evidence: Numbered locality in the Explanation of Thureau's 1881 goldfield map (PP 82/1881, reproduced Haygarth 2012 Fig.1). Nearest recorded gold occurrence today: ~8.4 km. Named for the 1875 wreck of the George Town Packet at the Pieman heads.

properties.name: Duck Creek
properties.tier: B — 1881-mapped gold locality, no modern record
properties.status_2026: EL2/2018 to Aug 2027; 213 m from mapped lead
properties.evidence: Numbered locality on Thureau's 1881 map; DUCK CREEK TRACK is a registered historic track name. Nearest recorded gold occurrence today: ~8.9 km.

properties.name: Mount Livingstone southern plateau
properties.tier: C — named terrace target, never systematised
properties.status_2026: EL23/2020 — lapses 2 Dec 2026; ~6 km from mapped Ts lead (terraces may be unmapped at 25K)
properties.evidence: Montgomery, Secretary of Mines Report 1893-94 (Haygarth 2022 n.29): 'there is undoubtedly an excellent field for hydraulic sluicing in the terraces along the Savage, Whyte, and Pieman Rivers, and on the plateau lying south of Mount Livingstone.' No occurrence within ~5 km of the plateau.

properties.name: Amelia Creek
properties.status_2026: not in the placenames register; archival relocation required
properties.evidence: Named by the Slater brothers with Nancy, Lucy and Alice Creeks (Haygarth 2012 p.61). Nancy and Lucy carry recorded gold workings; Amelia's name did not survive to the register. Trove 1879-85 papers are the relocation source.

properties.name: Alice Creek
properties.status_2026: not in the placenames register; archival relocation required
properties.evidence: As Amelia Creek: fourth of the Slater female-name set, name lost. Likely SE field near Nancy/Lucy Creeks.

properties.name: Lovers Falls paydirt (legend)
properties.status_2026: released area; adjacent to Donaldson Landing prospect
properties.evidence: Haygarth 2012 p.61: 'Lovers Falls (formerly True Lovers Falls) reputedly records the breach of trust when a lady's busy lips divulged the site of her lover's paydirt.' Folklore-grade evidence.
